title: Proteomic profiling of mouse tissues by data-independent acquisition (DIA) on Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Astral
projectDescription: This dataset presents proteomic profiles generated from four mouse tissues (brain, heart, liver, and lung) using a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer. Proteins were identified and quantified in a label-free manner via data-independent acquisition (DIA) LC–MS/MS, with the aim of establishing and validating the analytical workflow to be applied in our ongoing MARKOPOLO project.
sampleProcessingProtocol: 10-50 mg of the collected mouse tissue samples (brain, heart, liver, and lung) were homogenized in ice-cold lysis buffer (50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate [TEAB], 1% sodium deoxycholate [SDC], 10 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine [TCEP], and 40 mM 2-chloroacetamide) using either bead-based homogenization or Ultra-Turrax depending on the tissue type. Lysates were then incubated on ice for 30 min, denatured at 80 °C for 10 min (300 rpm), and sonicated with a QSonica Q125 Sonicator. Cell debris was removed by centrifugation at 15,000 × g for 15 min at 4°C, and the supernatant containing soluble proteins was collected. Protein concentrations were measured using a NanoPhotometer after 10-fold dilution using One-pot buffer as blank. The equivalent of 50 µg of protein was dried in a vacuum centrifuge, and resuspended in 100 µL digestion buffer (50 mM ammonium bicarbonate). Trypsin was added at a 1:50 ratio (1 µg) for overnight digestion at 37°C, followed by addition of trypsin at a 1:100 ratio (0.5 µg) and incubation for 1 hr at 37°C with gentle shaking. TFA (20% v/v) was added to a final concentration of 1% (v/v) and vortexed vigorously to ensure fast mixing and avoid protein precipitation, and pH was confirmed to be around pH 2. SDC precipitation was performed by mixing the samples at 1000 rpm for 5 min at 10°C, vortexing, and centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 5 min at 10°C. The supernatant containing the peptides was transferred to new low-binding tubes and stored frozen until use.   Liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) was performed in data-independent acquisition (DIA) mode on a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer coupled to an Evosep One LC system set to a standard setup (60 SPD) with a total runtime of 21 min. A total of 100 ng peptide per sample was desalted and loaded onto Evotip C18 columns following the manufacturer’s protocol and peptides were separated on an Evosep Endurance column (8 cm × 100 µm ID, 3.0 µm beads) with a 1000 nL/min gradient flow. Peptide samples were ionized via a nanospray ionization (NSI) source at +1.8 kV and transferred through a heated ion transfer tube maintained at 280 °C. Full MS scans were acquired in the Orbitrap at 240,000 resolution over an m/z range of 400–1000 using a 3 × 10⁶ AGC target and 5 ms maximum injection time. DIA MS/MS scans were collected across the 400–1000 m/z range using 2 m/z isolation windows (300 scan events total, 0.6 s cycle time) with a normalized collision energy of 30% (HCD) and Astral detector for high-speed fragment ion detection. Fragment ions were recorded at 140–2000 m/z in centroid mode with 3.5 ms maximum injection time. All data were acquired in positive polarity with advanced peak determination enabled and an expected LC peak width of 7s.
dataProcessingProtocol: To evaluate precursor- and protein-level FDR control, raw data files were processed in DIA-NN (version 2.3.2) using four distinct spectral library strategies. Library-free searches were performed directly against the target-plusentrapment FASTA database, whereas Prosit-, MS2PIP-, and Carafe-based searches used their respective predicted or empirically derived spectral libraries, with in-software FASTA-based library generation disabled in these cases. Precursor-level FDR was assessed using carbamidomethylation of cysteine as a fixed modification (no variable modifications applied), a peptide length range of 7–35 residues, and a precursor charge range of 2–4; the precursor-level FDR threshold was set to 10%, with N-terminal methionine excision disabled and all other parameters left at default settings. The 'Lib.Q.Value' metric was used as the precursor-level q-value for downstream analyses. Protein-level FDR was evaluated using the same peptide length and enzyme specificity settings as above, with the FDR threshold reduced to 1% and all remaining parameters matching the precursor-level analysis; the 'Lib.PG.Q.Value' metric was used as the protein-level q-value for downstream analyses.
